mainTopic: When the court forces a husband to divorce: blemishes, foul-smelling jobs, refusing support, and forbidden or childless marriages
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier topic. A wife's epilepsy counts as a hidden blemish only if the seizures come at fixed times. A new משנה teaches that a husband with blemishes is not forced to divorce, but רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says big blemishes, like a blinded eye or a cut-off hand, are grounds for forcing a divorce. The גמרא debates whether the משנה reads 'נולדו' or 'היו', explains why size matters even if she knew beforehand, and brings conflicting rulings on the הלכה. A second משנה lists men who must divorce: one with boils, one with a polyp, and men in smelly jobs. רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue whether a wife who agreed in advance can still back out. The גמרא defines the unclear words in that list. Then רב and שמואל argue whether a husband who refuses to support his wife must divorce her. Finally, the גמרא discusses whether בית דין forces divorce after ten childless years, and רבי אבא's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Epilepsy counts as a hidden blemish
steps.stepSummary: A woman who has epilepsy is treated like someone with a hidden blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: And an epileptic is considered like one with hidden blemishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the earlier discussion about a wife's blemishes by placing epilepsy in the 'hidden blemish' group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא separated blemishes people can see (מומין שבגלוי) from blemishes people cannot see (מומין שבסתר). Epilepsy is placed with the hidden ones, because others may not know about it.

keyTerms.meaning: An epileptic, a person who has seizures
Hidden blemishes that other people cannot see
Is considered like, is compared to

phrases.english: And an epileptic is considered like hidden blemishes.
phrases.notes: This continues the earlier talk about a wife's blemishes, so the epileptic here is the woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the previous daf's sorting of a wife's blemishes into hidden and visible ones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Epilepsy is treated as a hidden blemish (מום שבסתר).

steps.title: Only when the seizures come at fixed times
steps.stepSummary: Epilepsy is hidden only if the seizures come at set times. If they can come at any time, it counts as a visible blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only when it has a fixed time. But if it has no fixed time, it is considered like a visible blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the rule it just gave about epilepsy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seizures come on a schedule, the family can hide them, so the blemish stays hidden. If they can come at any moment, people will surely see them, so epilepsy then counts as a visible blemish (מום שבגלוי).

keyTerms.meaning: And this applies only... (a phrase that limits a rule)
It has a fixed, regular time
Visible blemishes that people can see

phrases.english: And this applies only when it has a fixed time,
phrases.notes: He means the seizures come at regular, predictable times.

phrases.english: but if it does not have a fixed time —
it is considered like visible blemishes.

steps.whatToRemember: Epilepsy is a hidden blemish only when the seizures come at fixed times. When they are unpredictable, it counts as a visible blemish.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of step 1 to seizures that come at fixed times.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seizures at fixed times count as a hidden blemish. Seizures with no fixed time count as a visible blemish.

steps.title: A husband with blemishes is not forced to divorce
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that a man who has blemishes is not forced by the court to divorce his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A man who developed blemishes is not forced to divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It moves from a wife's blemishes to a husband's blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the topic was a wife's blemishes. Now the משנה rules that a husband's blemishes do not give the court grounds to force a divorce. The word 'שנולדו' (that developed) will soon be argued over in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: To send her out, to divorce her

phrases.english: MISHNA: A man who developed blemishes —
we do not force him to divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאִישׁ שֶׁנּוֹלְדוּ בּוֹ מוּמִין אֵין כּוֹפִין אוֹתוֹ לְהוֹצִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about a husband's blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband's blemishes are not grounds for forcing him to divorce.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: big blemishes are different
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the rule covers only small blemishes. For big blemishes, the husband is forced to divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: When does this apply? With small blemishes. But with big blemishes, we force him to divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits the משנה's rule to small blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה said no husband is forced. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds a split: small blemishes are not grounds, but big blemishes are. This split becomes the key to the קשיא in Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case were these words said? (a phrase that limits a rule)

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
In what case are these words said?
With the small blemishes,
but with the big blemishes —
we force him to divorce.

steps.whyThisMatters: This big/small split is exactly what the גמרא uses later to challenge one reading of the משנה.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the first part of the משנה to small blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Small blemishes: no forced divorce. Big blemishes: the husband is forced to divorce.

steps.title: Two readings of the משנה: 'developed' or 'had'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reads the משנה as 'נולדו' (developed after the wedding). חייא בר רב reads it as 'היו' (he had them before the wedding).
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה teaches 'developed.' חייא בר רב teaches 'had.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two different versions of the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is over one word. 'נולדו' means the blemishes appeared after the marriage. 'היו' means he already had them when they married. Each reading describes a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Were, he had them (before the wedding)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda teaches 'developed.'
Ḥiyya bar Rav teaches 'had.'

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an argument about logic yet. It is about which word is actually written in the משנה. The logic comes in the next step.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה תָּנֵי נוֹלְדוּ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב תָּנֵי הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the exact wording of the משנה in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two versions of the משנה: 'נולדו' (רב יהודה) and 'היו' (חייא בר רב).

steps.title: What each reading implies
steps.stepSummary: The 'נולדו' reading includes 'היו' all the more, since she knew and accepted. The 'היו' reading means blemishes that appeared after the wedding are different.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 'developed' would hold all the more so for 'had,' since she knew and accepted. The one who says 'had' would hold: but 'developed,' no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what each version of the משנה means for the other case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even blemishes that appeared after the wedding do not force a divorce, then blemishes she saw and accepted before the wedding surely don't. But if the משנה is only about blemishes she knew about beforehand, then new blemishes she never agreed to might force a divorce.

phrases.english: The one who says 'developed,'
all the more so 'had' —
since she knew and accepted.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording, and both mean she knew.

phrases.english: The one who says 'had,'
but 'developed' — no.
phrases.notes: He means that if the blemishes appeared after the wedding, the husband may be forced to divorce.

steps.whatToRemember: 'נולדו' covers both cases: no forced divorce. 'היו' covers only blemishes she knew about, so blemishes that appeared after the wedding may force a divorce.
steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר נוֹלְדוּ כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what follows from each of the two readings in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to 'נולדו,' no forced divorce in either case. According to 'היו,' only blemishes from before the wedding are excluded.

steps.title: The big/small split fits only 'developed'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'היו' reading: if she knew about the blemishes and accepted them, why should big or small matter?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said, when does this apply? With small blemishes, but with big blemishes we force him to divorce. It works well for the one who says 'developed': that is why big and small are different. But for the one who says 'had,' what difference is big or small? She knew and accepted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words again, this time to use them as a challenge against חייא בר רב's reading 'היו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'נולדו,' the split makes sense: she never agreed to new blemishes, so big ones are grounds for divorce and small ones are not. With 'היו,' she saw the blemishes and agreed to marry him anyway, so even big blemishes should not let her demand a divorce. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's split seems to fit only the 'נולדו' reading.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well, granted (for one side)
What difference is it to me... or...

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן, אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: We learned: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
In what case are these words said?
With small blemishes,
but with big blemishes —
we force him to divorce.
It works well for the one who says 'developed,'
that is why big and small are different.
But for the one who says 'had' —

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי גְּדוֹלִים מָה לִי קְטַנִּים?
phrases.english: what difference is it to me, big or small?
She knew and accepted!

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not repeating the משנה just to review it. It quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל again so it can use his words as a weapon against the 'היו' reading.
steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר נוֹלְדוּ הַיְינוּ דְּשָׁאנֵי בֵּין גְּדוֹלִים לִקְטַנִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's big/small split from step 4 to attack the 'היו' reading from steps 5-6.
steps.kashyaTarget: חייא בר רב's reading 'היו' (the husband had the blemishes before the wedding).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the wife knew about the blemishes before the wedding and accepted them, the size of the blemish should not matter. So רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's split between big and small only makes sense if the blemishes appeared after the wedding.

steps.title: She thought she could handle it, but now she can't
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 7. With big blemishes, she can claim she thought she could live with them, but now she sees she cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: She thought she could accept it, but now she cannot accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering the question from Step 7: if she knew about the blemishes before the wedding, why does it matter whether they are big or small?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing about a blemish before the wedding is not the same as living with it every day. With small blemishes, her earlier acceptance still counts. With big blemishes, she can honestly say she misjudged how hard it would be, so the court forces him to divorce her.

keyTerms.meaning: To accept, to put up with

steps.whyThisMatters: This same claim, 'I thought I could accept it, but now I cannot,' comes back in רבי מאיר's words at the end of the new משנה.

phrases.english: She thought that she could accept [it],
but now she cannot accept [it].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes knowing about a blemish from actually living with it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If she knew about the blemishes and accepted them, big or small should make no difference.
steps.terutzMaskana: With big blemishes she can say she misjudged what she could handle, so her earlier acceptance does not hold.

steps.title: What counts as a big blemish?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which blemishes count as 'big' for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which are the big blemishes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next line by asking for a definition of 'big blemishes.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule depends on telling small blemishes apart from big ones, so we need to know where the line is.

phrases.english: And which are the big blemishes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the term used in Step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which blemishes count as 'big' for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל

steps.title: Examples of big blemishes
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives examples: a blinded eye, a hand that was cut off, or a broken leg.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל explained: for example, his eye was blinded, his hand was cut off, or his leg was broken.
steps.whatsHappening: The question from Step 9 is answered with examples given by רבן שמעון בן גמליאל himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three examples are serious injuries to a major part of the body. These are the kind of blemishes where the court forces the husband to divorce her.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel explained:
for example, his eye was blinded,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: his hand was cut off, or his leg was broken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of Step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Big blemishes are things like a blinded eye, a hand cut off, or a broken leg.

steps.title: Two rulings on whose view is the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר יעקב reports that רבי יוחנן rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רבא reports that רב נחמן rules like the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי אבא בר יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: the הלכה follows the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two opposite rulings on the practical הלכה in the argument about big and small blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, big blemishes are grounds for forcing a divorce. According to רב נחמן, the court never forces a divorce over a husband's blemishes, big or small.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (here, the first opinion in the משנה)

phrases.aramaic: אִתְּמַר, רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Abba bar Yaakov said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
Rava said that Rav Nachman said:
The halacha follows the words of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר, רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the opinions to ruling on the practical הלכה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל; רב נחמן rules like the חכמים.

steps.title: Why would רבי יוחנן need to say this here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the report in רבי יוחנן's name. רבי יוחנן already has a general rule that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in our משנה except in three places, so why rule on this case separately?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: wherever רבן שמעון בן גמליאל taught in our משנה, the הלכה follows him, except in the cases of the guarantor, צידן, and the last ruling about evidence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ruling that רבי אבא בר יעקב reported in רבי יוחנן's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוחנן already said the הלכה always follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה except in three cases, our case is already covered. A separate ruling for it seems unnecessary, so the report looks doubtful.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say so? (opens a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not questioning whether the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Both reports agree on that. The question is why רבי יוחנן would need to say it specifically here.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan say this?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁשָּׁנָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּמִשְׁנָתֵנוּ —
phrases.english: Wherever Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel taught in our Mishnah,
the halacha follows him,
except for the guarantor, Sidon, and the last [ruling about] evidence.
phrases.notes: These are three other places in the משנה where he speaks: a case about a guarantor, a divorce case in צידן, and his last argument about evidence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first ruling in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in this specific case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's general rule already covers this case, so a separate ruling would be unnecessary.

steps.title: The אמוראים report רבי יוחנן differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אבא בר יעקב and רבה בר בר חנה are two אמוראים who disagree about what רבי יוחנן held.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are אמוראים, and they disagree about what רבי יוחנן said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in Step 12 by saying that two different reports of רבי יוחנן's teaching are being compared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר בר חנה reports a general rule from רבי יוחנן. רבי אבא בר יעקב does not hold that רבי יוחנן gave that general rule, so he reports a separate ruling for this case. Each report fits its own tradition, so nothing contradicts.

phrases.english: They are [two] Amoraim,
and [they disagree] about the view of Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two students report the same teacher differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both reports come from one tradition, so a separate ruling would be unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each אמורא has his own version of רבי יוחנן's view, so each report is consistent on its own terms.

steps.title: New משנה: men who are forced to divorce
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists men the court forces to divorce their wives: one with boils, one with a polyp, and men who work at foul-smelling jobs. This applies whether the problem existed before the marriage or began after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These are the men who are forced to divorce: one with boils, one with a polyp, a gatherer, a copper smelter, and a tanner. This applies whether these existed before they married or began after they married.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists cases where the court forces the husband to give a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier משנה, where blemishes alone are not enough, these problems are severe enough that the court forces a divorce. It makes no difference whether he had them before the wedding or they came later.

keyTerms.meaning: The court forces him to divorce
A polyp (a growth that causes a bad smell)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the previous משנה. There, blemishes were not enough to force a divorce. Here, these specific cases are.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: And these are [the men] whom [the court] forces to divorce:
one afflicted with boils, and one who has a polyp,
and a gatherer, and a copper smelter, and a tanner.
Whether they existed before they married,
or whether they began after they married.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of blemishes
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court forces a divorce for boils, a polyp, and foul-smelling jobs, whether these existed before the marriage or began after it.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: even a warning in advance does not help
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says that even if the husband told her about the problem before the wedding, she can still say, 'I thought I could accept it, but now I cannot.'
steps.simpleTranslation: About all of these, רבי מאיר said: even though he made a condition with her, she can say, 'I thought I could accept it, but now I cannot accept it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר adds a further point to the list in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if she agreed in advance, her agreement does not stop her from demanding a divorce. She can claim that living with the problem turned out to be more than she could handle.

keyTerms.meaning: He made a condition with her (told her in advance)

steps.whatToRemember: Agreeing ahead of time does not always lock a wife in. For serious problems, she can say, 'I thought I could accept it, but now I cannot.' This is the same reasoning the גמרא used for big blemishes in Step 8.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא's answer in Step 8, explaining רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, uses this same wording: 'she thought she could accept it, but now she cannot.'

phrases.english: And about all of them, Rabbi Meir said:
even though he made a condition with her,
she can say:
"I thought that I could accept [it],
but now I cannot accept [it]."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי מאיר's ruling about a condition made before the wedding
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even if he told her in advance, she can demand a divorce by saying she thought she could accept it but now cannot.

steps.title: The חכמים: She Must Accept It, Except for Boils
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue with רבי מאיר. If the wife accepted the problem, she is stuck with it. The only exception is a מוכה שחין, because relations harm him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: she must accept it against her will, except for a man with boils, because it makes his body waste away.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the חכמים's side against רבי מאיר. If she agreed to the problem before marriage, she cannot back out later, except in the case of boils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said she can always say 'I thought I could handle it.' The חכמים say her agreement binds her. Boils are different because marital relations physically harm the husband, so he must divorce her anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: That she makes him waste away (his flesh rots)

steps.confusionAlert: The boils exception is not about her comfort. It exists because staying together harms the husband's own body.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
She must accept it against her will,
phrases.notes: This means only if she agreed to it before the wedding, which is רבי מאיר's case from the last step.

phrases.english: except for one afflicted with boils,
because she makes him waste away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר's ruling in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife who agreed to the defect must accept it, except for a husband with boils.

steps.title: The Story of the Tanner's Widow in צידן
steps.stepSummary: A tanner died childless and his brother, also a tanner, was the יבם. The חכמים ruled she can refuse him. She accepted the smell for her husband, but not for his brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident in צידן with a tanner who died, and his brother was also a tanner. The חכמים said she can say: 'I could accept it for your brother, but I cannot accept it for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a story. Even though the widow agreed to live with one tanner, she does not have to do יבום with his brother, who is also a tanner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her earlier acceptance was personal, toward her husband only. It does not carry over to a different man with the same smelly job, so the brother must do חליצה instead.

keyTerms.meaning: A tanner, who works hides and smells bad

steps.whatToRemember: Agreeing to one man's defect does not mean agreeing to the same defect in another man.

phrases.english: There was an incident in Sidon
with a certain tanner who died,
and he had a brother who was a tanner.
phrases.notes: He died without children, so this brother was supposed to marry the widow through יבום.

phrases.english: The Sages said:
She can say:
"For your brother I could accept it,
but for you I cannot accept it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story that shows a limit on the wife's acceptance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow can refuse יבום with a tanner brother even though she lived with a tanner husband.

steps.title: What Is a בעל פוליפוס?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking what the משנה's word פוליפוס means.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is 'one with a polyp'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion. It asks for the meaning of an unclear word in the משנה and sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed a בעל פוליפוס without explaining the term. The גמרא wants to know exactly which defect it means.

keyTerms.meaning: One with a polyp, a growth that causes a bad smell

phrases.english: Gemara: What is "one with a polyp"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא's explanation of its words.

steps.title: Nose Smell or Mouth Smell
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says it is a bad smell from the nose. A ברייתא says it is a bad smell from the mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in שמואל's name: a bad smell from the nose. A ברייתא taught: a bad smell from the mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two answers to what פוליפוס means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers agree it is a foul smell. They differ on where it comes from: שמואל says the nose, the ברייתא says the mouth.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A bad smell from the nose.
In a baraita it was taught:
A bad smell from the mouth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל: nose odor. ברייתא: mouth odor.

steps.title: רב אסי Reverses It, With a Memory Sign
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי reports it the other way around: שמואל said mouth. He gives a memory sign: 'שמואל never closed his mouth from our chapter.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי teaches the opposite. He gave a memory sign: שמואל did not stop his mouth from our whole chapter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of who said what, plus a sign to help remember it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב אסי's version, שמואל holds 'mouth' and the ברייתא holds 'nose.' The sign uses the word 'mouth' (פומיה) next to שמואל's name, so you remember that שמואל said mouth.

phrases.english: Rav Asi teaches it the opposite way.
phrases.notes: For him, שמואל is the one who said 'mouth.'

phrases.english: And he set a memory sign for it:
Shmuel did not close his mouth
from our entire chapter.
phrases.notes: He means שמואל talked about this chapter a lot. The word 'mouth' links שמואל with the mouth opinion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a reversed version of the attributions in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב אסי's version, שמואל holds that פוליפוס is a mouth odor.

steps.title: What Is a מקמץ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's word מקמץ and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the gatherer.' What is a gatherer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next unclear word in the משנה's list and sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מקמץ is one of the smelly jobs in the משנה. The גמרא needs to define exactly what this worker does.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'gatherer', one of the smelly jobs in the משנה

phrases.english: "And the gatherer."
What is a "gatherer"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next term in the משנה.

steps.title: רב יהודה: A Collector of Dog Excrement
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that a מקמץ is someone who collects dog excrement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: This is one who collects dog excrement.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question about the word מקמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads מקמץ as related to מקבץ, 'gathering.' That makes it a separate job that involves collecting something foul.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
This is one who collects dog excrement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מקמץ is a collector of dog excrement.

steps.title: A ברייתא Says a מקמץ Is a Tanner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה from a ברייתא that defines מקמץ as a tanner.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: 'A gatherer is a tanner!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יהודה's definition with a ברייתא that says something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא like רב יהודה should not disagree with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says a מקמץ is a tanner, not a dog-excrement collector.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"A gatherer, this is a tanner!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא defines מקמץ as a tanner, which contradicts רב יהודה.

steps.title: But the משנה Itself Lists Them Separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers back: the ברייתא has its own problem, because the משנה lists מקמץ and בורסי as two different jobs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, the משנה should be difficult for you: 'the gatherer, the copper smelter, and the tanner'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the challenge around. It points out that the ברייתא seems to clash with the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a מקמץ is a tanner, why would the משנה name both of them in the same list? The point is that the ברייתא has its own clash with the משנה. That problem is not unique to רב יהודה, so the challenge from the ברייתא is weakened.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
the Mishnah should be difficult for you:
"the gatherer, and the copper smelter, and the tanner"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A counter-challenge showing the ברייתא clashes with the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's definition of מקמץ as a tanner.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists מקמץ and בורסי separately, so they cannot be the same job.

steps.title: Big Tanner Versus Small Tanner
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא and משנה can fit together. The משנה's 'tanner' is a large-scale tanner, and the ברייתא's מקמץ is a small-scale tanner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, the משנה is not difficult: here it is a large tanner, there it is a small tanner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא can be squared with the משנה by splitting 'tanner' into two sizes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's separate בורסי is a big tanner. The ברייתא's מקמץ is a small tanner. So the two sources do not really conflict.

phrases.english: Granted, the Mishnah is not difficult:
here it is a large tanner,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the משנה, which lists the big tanner separately.

phrases.english: there it is a small tanner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the counter-challenge of Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between cases (large vs. small tanner)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא contradicts the משנה, so it cannot be used against רב יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא fits the משנה if its מקמץ is a small tanner.

steps.title: The Challenge to רב יהודה Returns
steps.stepSummary: Now that the ברייתא fits the משנה, the original problem against רב יהודה comes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב יהודה, it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the challenge from Step 23 and sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא no longer has a problem of its own. So it still says a מקמץ is a tanner, against רב יהודה.

phrases.english: But according to Rav Yehuda, it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restores the challenge of Step 23 after Step 25 cleared the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא, now fully consistent, still defines מקמץ as a tanner.

steps.title: It Is a Dispute Between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תנאים already disagreed about this. One view says a tanner, and a יש אומרים says a dog-excrement collector, like רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute of תנאים, as it was taught: 'A gatherer is a tanner. And some say: this is one who gathers dog excrement.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יהודה by showing that a תנא agrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used against רב יהודה is only one opinion. Another opinion in the same ברייתא says exactly what רב יהודה said, so he is following that תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים

steps.whatToRemember: An אמורא challenged by a ברייתא can be defended if another תנא agrees with him. Here רב יהודה follows the יש אומרים.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tannaim, as it was taught:
"A gatherer, this is a tanner,
and some say:
this is one who gathers dog excrement."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the restored challenge of Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: תנאי היא: the אמורא follows one side of a dispute between תנאים
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יהודה follows the יש אומרים in the ברייתא.

steps.title: What is a coppersmith?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה and asks what מצרף נחושת means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And the coppersmith and the tanner.' What is a 'coppersmith'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next job in the משנה's list and asks what kind of worker a מצרף נחושת is. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists smelly jobs that can let a wife demand a divorce. The words מצרף נחושת are unclear: it could mean someone who works copper into pots, or someone who digs it out. The גמרא wants a clear definition.

keyTerms.meaning: a coppersmith, a copper worker (exact meaning is being asked)

phrases.english: And the coppersmith and the tanner.
What is a 'coppersmith'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the discussion of מקמץ, the גמרא moves to the next job in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact meaning of מצרף נחושת.

steps.title: רב אשי: a kettle smith
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says a מצרף נחושת is a smith who hammers out copper kettles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is a kettle smith.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the first answer: the coppersmith is someone who beats copper into kettles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב אשי, the smell comes from working copper into pots. This is a craftsman who shapes the metal, not someone who mines it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Kettle smiths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in Step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מצרף נחושת is one who hammers copper into kettles.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה: one who cuts copper from its source
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה says a מצרף נחושת is someone who cuts copper out of the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: This is one who cuts copper from its source.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer is given: the coppersmith is a person who cuts raw copper out at its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר בר חנה places the job earlier in the process, at mining the raw metal. So the two answers disagree about which copper worker the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: from its source, from its root

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥanna said:
This is one who cuts copper from its source.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same question from Step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מצרף נחושת is one who cuts copper from its source.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבה בר בר חנה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines מצרף exactly as רבה בר בר חנה did.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with רבה בר בר חנה: Who is a 'coppersmith'? This is one who cuts copper from its source.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses the same words as רבה בר בר חנה, which backs up his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא is a source from the תנאים, so it carries extra weight. Since it matches רבה בר בר חנה word for word, his definition gets support. רב אשי is not refuted outright, but the ברייתא sides with the other view.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא in line with him

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on מצרף נחושת: רב אשי says a kettle smith, and רבה בר בר חנה says one who cuts copper from its source. A ברייתא supports רבה בר בר חנה.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה:
phrases.english: It was taught in line with Rabba bar bar Ḥanna:
Who is a 'coppersmith'?
This is one who cuts copper from its source.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 30 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבה בר בר חנה's definition of מצרף נחושת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that defines מצרף as one who cuts copper from its source.

steps.title: רב: a husband who refuses to support his wife must divorce her
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a husband who says he will not feed or support his wife must divorce her and pay her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: One who says, 'I will not feed and I will not support,' must divorce her and give her the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about forcing a divorce: if a husband refuses to support his wife, he must divorce her and pay her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה dealt with cases where the husband is forced to divorce. רב adds another case: a husband who openly refuses to provide for his wife. רב's solution is divorce, not forcing him to pay support.

keyTerms.meaning: he must divorce (literally, send her out)
the payment promised to a wife in her marriage contract

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: הָאוֹמֵר ״אֵינִי זָן וְאֵינִי מְפַרְנֵס״
phrases.english: Rav said: One who says, 'I will not feed and I will not support'
must divorce her and give her the marriage contract payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: הָאוֹמֵר ״אֵינִי זָן וְאֵינִי מְפַרְנֵס״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic linked to the משנה's theme of forcing a divorce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband who refuses to feed and support his wife must divorce her and pay the כתובה.

steps.title: שמואל: better to force him to support her
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר repeats רב's ruling to שמואל, who mocks it and says בית דין should force the husband to support her instead of forcing a divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר went and said this teaching before שמואל. שמואל said: Feed אלעזר barley! Rather than forcing him to divorce, let them force him to feed her.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל strongly disagrees with רב's ruling. He argues that if בית דין can force the husband to divorce, it can just as easily force him to provide food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's challenge is simple logic: forcing a divorce is the harsher step. If the problem is lack of support, the direct fix is to force support. So why break up the marriage?

keyTerms.meaning: feed him barley (a sharp way of calling something nonsense)

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אַמְרַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar went and said the teaching before Shmuel.
He said: Feed Elazar barley!
phrases.notes: Barley is animal food. שמואל is saying this ruling is nonsense.

phrases.english: Rather than forcing him to divorce,
let them force him to feed her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling from Step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the husband must divorce.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If בית דין can force a divorce, it can force support, which fixes the actual problem without ending the marriage.

steps.title: רב's reason: no one lives with a snake in a basket
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רב's view: a woman cannot be expected to live closely with a husband who supports her only under force.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how would רב answer? A person does not live with a snake in a basket.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב would answer שמואל, and gives רב's reason with a short saying about a snake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forcing the husband to pay does not fix the marriage. A man who openly refuses to support his wife is like a snake, and she cannot be asked to share close quarters with him. So divorce is the right solution.

phrases.english: And Rav?
phrases.notes: Short for: how would רב answer שמואל's question?

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם דָּר עִם נָחָשׁ בִּכְפִיפָה.
phrases.english: A person does not live with a snake in a basket.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב: אֵין אָדָם דָּר עִם נָחָשׁ בִּכְפִיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב against שמואל's challenge in Step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reasoning behind רב's ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forcing support should be enough, so divorce is unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Forced support does not let her live in peace with such a husband, so divorce is required.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן also holds like רב
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל, רבי זירא hears רב's ruling taught in the name of רבי יוחנן, and remarks that אלעזר was mocked in בבל for this very ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא went up to ארץ ישראל, he found רבי בנימין בר יפת sitting and teaching it in the name of רבי יוחנן. He said to him: For this they fed אלעזר barley in בבל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing that רבי יוחנן taught the same ruling as רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling שמואל mocked turns out to be taught by רבי יוחנן, the great teacher of ארץ ישראל. This gives רב's view strong support. רבי זירא's comment points out the irony that the same ruling was laughed at in בבל.
steps.whatToRemember: רב, and also רבי יוחנן, rule that a husband who refuses to support his wife must divorce her. שמואל says force him to support her. רב's reason: she cannot live with a 'snake.'

phrases.english: When Rabbi Zeira went up,
he found Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet

phrases.aramaic: דְּיָתֵיב וְקָאָמַר לַהּ, מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן.
phrases.english: sitting and saying it, in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan.
phrases.notes: 'It' is רב's ruling that the husband must divorce her.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַל דָּא אַכְּסוּהּ שְׂעָרִין לְאֶלְעָזָר בְּבָבֶל.
phrases.english: He said to him: For this they fed Elazar barley in Babylonia!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds support for רב's ruling after defending it in Step 34.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that a husband who refuses support must divorce.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's teaching, reported by רבי בנימין בר יפת.

steps.title: רב אסי: forcing divorce only for forbidden wives
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב אסי: בית דין forces divorce only when the wife is forbidden to the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב אסי: They force a divorce only for forbidden wives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule about when בית דין forces a husband to divorce: only when the marriage is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This limits forced divorce to marriages that are not allowed in the first place. The word פסולות is general, so the next step will explain which women are meant.

keyTerms.meaning: women forbidden to marry this husband

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav Asi said:
They force a divorce only for forbidden wives.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling on the topic of forcing a divorce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית דין forces divorce only when the wife is forbidden to the husband.

steps.title: שמואל lists the forbidden marriages
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains פסולות with examples of marriages the תורה forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said it before שמואל, he said: For example, a widow to a כהן גדול, a divorcée or a חלוצה to a regular כהן, a ממזרת or נתינה to a ישראל, a בת ישראל to a נתין or a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה reports that שמואל explained which 'forbidden wives' רב אסי meant, by giving a list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every case on the list is a marriage the תורה forbids, either because of כהונה rules or because of ממזר and נתין status. These are the marriages where בית דין steps in to force a divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: a widow released from יבום through חליצה
a woman born from a forbidden relationship
a woman descended from the גבעונים

phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel, he said:
phrases.notes: 'I' is רב יהודה, who quoted רב אסי's rule to שמואל.

phrases.english: For example, a widow to a High Priest,
and a divorcée or a ḥalutza to a common priest,
a mamzeret or a Gibeonite woman to an Israelite,
an Israelite woman to a Gibeonite or to a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word פסולות from Step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'forbidden wives' are those the תורה forbids to the husband, like a widow to a כהן גדול or a ממזרת to a ישראל.

steps.title: No forced divorce after ten childless years
steps.stepSummary: שמואל adds that if a man was married ten years without children, בית דין does not force him to divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he married a woman and stayed with her ten years and she did not give birth, they do not force him.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל finishes by saying which case is not included: a marriage with no children after ten years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though such a man is not fulfilling the מצוה of having children, his marriage itself is not forbidden. Since רב אסי's rule covers only forbidden marriages, בית דין does not force a divorce here.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean having no children for ten years is unimportant. It only means בית דין does not force a divorce in this case, since the marriage itself is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אסי: בית דין forces divorce only for forbidden marriages. שמואל: these are marriages the תורה forbids, but not a couple who have had no children for ten years.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נָשָׂא אִשָּׁה וְשָׁהָה עִמָּהּ עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים
phrases.english: But if he married a woman and stayed with her ten years
and she did not give birth,
they do not force him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל נָשָׂא אִשָּׁה וְשָׁהָה עִמָּהּ עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes שמואל's explanation by stating what is not included in רב אסי's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband married ten years without children is not forced to divorce.

steps.title: A different report of שמואל: after ten childless years, they do force him
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא בר אבימי reports in the name of שמואל that if a man was married ten years and his wife had no children, בית דין forces him to divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא בר אבימי said in the name of שמואל: even if a man married a woman, stayed with her ten years, and she had no children, the court forces him to divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of what שמואל said, and it is the exact opposite of the report in the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 38, שמואל was quoted as saying בית דין does not force a divorce after ten childless years. Here רב תחליפא בר אבימי quotes שמואל as saying בית דין does force it. This means force is used even in a marriage that is not forbidden, which sets up the question from the משנה in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Stayed with her (lived married to her)
They force him (בית דין compels him to divorce)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two opposite reports of שמואל in a row. Step 38 says they do not force him. This step says they do force him. Keep the two versions apart.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אֲבִימִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: And Rav Tachalifa bar Avimi said that Shmuel said:
Even if he married a woman
and stayed with her ten years
and she did not give birth,
they force him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אֲבִימִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite version of שמואל's ruling from step 38.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After ten childless years of marriage, בית דין forces the husband to divorce.

steps.title: Why doesn't the משנה list the childless case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה, which lists cases where בית דין forces a divorce. That list fits רב אסי, but if רב תחליפא is right, the משנה should also have listed the ten-year childless case.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: these are the men who are forced to divorce: one with boils and one with a polyp. According to רב אסי this makes sense, because the משנה lists only rabbinic cases and not cases from the תורה. But according to רב תחליפא בר אבימי, the משנה should also list the man who was married ten years without children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב תחליפא בר אבימי's version from the משנה: if the childless case is also forced, why isn't it on the משנה's list?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אסי there is no problem. The משנה lists the rabbinic cases, like boils and a polyp. It leaves out the Torah cases, the forbidden marriages of steps 36-37. But a ten-year childless marriage is not a forbidden marriage, so it should have been listed next to boils and a polyp, and it was not.

keyTerms.meaning: A man afflicted with boils (a skin disease)
A man with a polyp (causes a bad smell)
It works well (according to one opinion), used before raising a problem for the other opinion
Let it teach (it should have said)

phrases.english: We learned in the Mishnah:
These are the ones they force to divorce:
one afflicted with boils, and one with a polyp.
Granted, according to Rav Asi:
it teaches the rabbinic cases,
the Torah cases it does not teach.
phrases.notes: The cases from the תורה are the forbidden marriages from steps 36-37. רב אסי said force is used for those.

phrases.english: But according to Rav Tachalifa bar Avimi,
let it teach: he married a woman
and stayed with her ten years
and she did not give birth, they force him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 39 using the list in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב תחליפא בר אבימי's version of שמואל (step 39)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists the non-Torah cases where force is used. The childless case is also a non-Torah case, so if force were used there, the משנה should have listed it.

steps.title: רב נחמן: one is forced with words, the other with rods
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that there are two kinds of forcing. In the childless case בית דין pushes only with words. In the משנה's cases it forces with rods.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: this is no problem. One case is with words, the other is with rods.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question by saying the two cases are forced in different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the childless case, בית דין only pressures the husband with words. The משנה lists only cases where they use real physical force (rods). That is why the childless case is not on the משנה's list.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (there is no contradiction)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: It is not difficult:
this is with words,
phrases.notes: This is the ten-year childless case. בית דין only pushes him by talking.

phrases.english: that is with rods.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's list, where they actually beat him until he agrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 40.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (two different levels of forcing)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases are forced in the same way, so the משנה should list both.
steps.terutzMaskana: The childless case uses only words, while the משנה lists only cases forced with rods.

steps.title: רבי אבא: words alone do not work
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא objects to רב נחמן with a פסוק that says a servant is not corrected by words. Pushing with words alone is not real forcing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא objected: the פסוק says, "A servant will not be corrected by words"!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא attacks רב נחמן's answer by quoting a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said the childless case is forced with words. But the פסוק teaches that words alone do not make a stubborn person obey. So talking cannot be the kind of forcing that רב תחליפא בר אבימי's ruling means.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (a strong challenge)
A servant will not be corrected by words (משלי 29:19)

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba objected to this:
"A servant will not be corrected by words"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's answer in step 41.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's idea that the childless case is forced with words only
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows that words alone do not get someone to obey, so verbal pressure is not real forcing.

steps.title: רבי אבא starts a new answer: both cases use rods
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא gives his own answer: in both the משנה's cases and the childless case, בית דין forces with rods. His full explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אבא said: both this and that are with rods,
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא drops רב נחמן's answer and begins his own. The sentence is not finished here, and the גמרא continues it on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא agrees that the childless case is forced with rods, just like the משנה's cases. So he still has to explain some other difference between them, and that explanation comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (setting aside the earlier answer for a new one)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אבא's answer is not finished yet. Saying both use rods does not answer the question by itself. The rest of his answer comes next.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Abba said:
both this and that are with rods,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: הָא וְהָא בְּשׁוֹטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב נחמן's rejected answer with a new answer to step 40.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New way of splitting the cases (continues past this section)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן thought the difference was words versus rods.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases use rods, and the real difference is explained next.
